key_terms.meaning: Classic 3-stage ARM core with Thumb, debug, multiplier and embedded ICE; often used to teach core ARM concepts.
Four-bit field in most ARM instructions that decides execution from the N, Z, C and V flags.
Pipeline stage that reads the next instruction from memory into the CPU.
Pipeline stage that interprets the instruction and reads its source registers.
Pipeline stage that performs the ALU, memory or branch action.
ARM-state instructions are all 32 bits long, so fetch and decode are regular.
Only load and store instructions move data between registers and memory; ALU instructions work register-to-register.
The programmer sees 16 general registers R0-R15; banked registers appear in exception modes.
Memory order that stores the most significant byte of a word at the lowest byte address.
Memory order that stores the least significant byte of a word at the lowest byte address.
Current Program Status Register: holds condition flags, interrupt masks, mode bits and the T state bit.
Five CPSR bits that select the current processor mode.
CPSR bit that selects Thumb state when 1 and ARM state when 0.
CPSR condition flags N for negative, Z for zero, C for carry or borrow, and V for overflow.
CPSR interrupt mask bits; I masks IRQ and F masks FIQ when set.
Fixed low or high memory addresses that hold exception handler entry addresses.
16-bit encoding of a subset of ARM instructions that improves code density.
Rules such as AAPCS for argument passing, return values, stack use and register preservation between C and assembly.
Nested Vectored Interrupt Controller in Cortex-M that handles interrupts with priorities and vectoring.
Power-saving method that stops the clock to idle logic while keeping its state and power.

takeaways: ARM is a load-store RISC design: only LDR and STR access memory, while ALU instructions use registers.
Fixed 32-bit ARM instructions and a simple pipeline trade code size for regular fetch, decode and execute.
The programmer's model has R0-R15 plus CPSR; exception modes bank some registers and save state.
Seven ARM exceptions use fixed vectors; entry switches mode and saves return state.
Almost every ARM instruction can be conditional, which removes many short branches.
Thumb gives 16-bit encodings of common operations and improves code density on small memories.
C and assembly interoperate safely only when both follow AAPCS and preserve callee-saved registers.
Cortex-M adds NVIC and Thumb-2; ARM7TDMI is a classic 3-stage von Neumann teaching core.
Average current falls with clock gating, power gating and sleep modes between work bursts.
bank_note: The syllabi stress long answers that connect ARM's load-store RISC design and programmer's model to exceptions, instruction formats, Thumb, Cortex-M differences and low-power design.

glossary.def: Reduced Instruction Set Computer design with simple regular instructions, many registers and load-store memory access.
Complex Instruction Set Computer design with richer variable-length instructions and more memory operands.
CPU design in which only load and store instructions access memory; arithmetic uses registers.
Overlapped execution of instruction stages so several instructions are in progress at once.
Three basic pipeline stages: read instruction, interpret it and perform its operation.
Small fast storage inside the CPU named R0-R15 in the ARM programmer's model.
Register R15 that holds the address of the instruction being fetched or the next instruction.
Register R13 used by convention to point to the current top of the stack.
Register R14 that holds the return address after a branch with link.
Current Program Status Register holding flags, interrupt masks, mode bits and the T bit.
Saved Program Status Register used in exception modes to preserve the previous CPSR.
Event such as reset, undefined instruction, SWI, abort, IRQ or FIQ that changes processor mode and control flow.
Asynchronous exception, IRQ or FIQ, raised by hardware.
Table of fixed addresses containing handler entry addresses for exceptions.
Operating state selected by CPSR mode bits that determines visible banked registers and privileges.
ARM Architecture Procedure Call Standard for register use, arguments, stack alignment and preservation.
Mixed 16-bit and 32-bit instruction set used in Cortex-M cores for code density and performance.
Computer organization with separate instruction and data buses or memories.
Computer organization with a shared instruction and data memory and bus.
Byte order in memory: little-endian puts the least significant byte first; big-endian puts the most significant byte first.
Nested Vectored Interrupt Controller in Cortex-M that prioritizes and dispatches interrupts.
Stopping the clock to a block to save dynamic power while keeping its state.
Disconnecting power from a block to save leakage power; state is lost unless saved.
Low-power state in which the CPU clock stops and wakes on an interrupt or event.
